title: Correcting congenital myasthenia-associated acetylcholine receptor defects.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened PDB (Protein Data Bank) entry 9YE6 metadata via the RCSB API: a 2.47 Å cryo-EM (cryogenic electron microscopy) structure of human muscle acetylcholine receptor CMS (congenital myasthenic syndrome) mutants, citing this paper. A PDB full-text search on the DOI returned 12 entries; Europe PMC text-mining lists 14 PDB IDs (9DMG, 9DMH, 9YE6–9YF0).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about mutant identities, drugs tested and electrophysiology results comes from the abstract only; full text returned an error and the supplement endpoint gave no zip, so no per-mutant functional table was seen.

a1_downloadable.note: PDB/EMDB (Electron Microscopy Data Bank) structures are openly downloadable; checked 9YE6 metadata. Electrophysiology tables were not retrievable (supplement unavailable).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No tabular label exists in what was found: the deposits are 3D structures, and any functional label (gating change, drug block) would have to be extracted by hand from figures or a supplement that could not be retrieved.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequences and coordinates are in the PDB entries.

a4_units_stated.note: No label table seen, so units cannot be verified.

a5_enough_rows.note: 12–14 structures of a handful of representative mutants and drug complexes (counted via PDB search and text-mined IDs); far below the ~400-row minimum.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: PDB search (12) and text-mined IDs (14) are consistent once two likely earlier or related entries are allowed for; not material.

a8_label_provenance.note: Structures and patch-clamp recordings are physical measurements, not model outputs.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (would apply to variant-effect prediction, not to this dataset)

integration.partner_dataset: ClinVar or a CHRNA1/CHRNE deep mutational scan, if one exists (not searched)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Whether fast- versus slow-channel CMS mutations can be predicted from sequence and structure, but this paper supplies only a few labelled mutants.

honest_claim_h3: With about a dozen structures of a few mutants, no model could make a claim; the data supports mechanistic structural biology, not ML.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use receptor mutation sequence and structure to predict whether a muscle acetylcholine receptor mutation speeds up or slows down channel opening.
plain_idea.train_on: Mutant acetylcholine receptor structures and sequences; about 12–14 deposited structures covering a handful of mutants.
plain_idea.predict: Fast-channel versus slow-channel defect, or drug response, measured by single-channel electrophysiology in the paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinicians diagnosing congenital myasthenia choose drugs by channel type, but this paper has far too few mutants to train anything.

ml_idea: Classify CMS acetylcholine receptor mutations as fast- versus slow-channel from sequence/structure; infeasible here because only a few representative mutants were studied.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; project fails on sample size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count deposited structures/mutants: 12–14 PDB entries, done.

verdict_reason: Cryo-EM structural paper with 12–14 PDB structures of a few representative mutants; no tabular label (A2) and far too few examples (A5).
